predictions.P1: uniform refinement: |k_h^2 - k^2| prop N^(-4/9) asymptotically (|||e|||^2 ~ h^(4/3) from H ~ r^(-1/3); N prop h^-3); pre-asymptotic slopes between -4/9 and -2/3.
predictions.P2: Dorfler-adaptive (residual or ZZ): prop N^(-2/3) asymptotically. Equidistribution count: per-element error^2 ~ h^5 r^(2 alpha - 4), alpha = 2/3; h(r) ~ delta^(1/5) r^((4 - 2 alpha)/5); N ~ int h^-3 r dr is finite iff alpha > 1/3, so isotropic refinement of this edge singularity recovers the smooth rate.
predictions.P3: at equal N the uniform/adaptive error ratio grows like N^(2/9) (about 2.1 after a 30x growth from equal error).
predictions.P4: random marking with the adaptive run's per-iteration counts behaves like uniform refinement and loses to Dorfler.
predictions.P5: a-priori geometric marking (distance to the re-entrant edge, same counts) is close to Dorfler on this geometry; the estimator's value is not needing to know where the singularity is.
predictions.P6: explicit time domain: the adapted mesh's Voronoi dt_max is smaller than that of the uniform mesh of equal eigenvalue error (dt prop h_min); report N/dt for both (adaptivity is not free in the time domain; LTS exists).
predictions.P7: the residual effectivity eta/|||e||| on the box (§5 E3) is constant to within the level-ratio band across similar Kuhn meshes; eta_ZZ / ||curl e|| is close to 1 there.
